title: runtime-kernel-regression-deltas
body:
Executive summary:

We ran a focused regression sweep to validate three recent runtime kernel changes ahead of onboarding the Llama-2-13B family for Dedicated/Private customers: (1) upgraded FlashAttention v2 kernels, (2) paged KV cache with 64KB/256KB page sizes, and (3) continuous-batching heuristic that aggregates inflight tokens for 15ms windows. Purpose: detect functional regressions and quantify quality vs. latency tradeoffs on large prompt sets used in model onboarding/evals.

High-level findings (short):
- FlashAttention v2: ~18–25% token throughput improvement for short/medium sequences, median latency down 12% p50; however we observed a small (~0.9%) drop in long-context next-token accuracy on our conversation continuation eval (see diffs). Root cause traced to attention dropout seed handling when combined with mixed-precision reorder in one microkernel.
- Paged KV: 256KB page size produced stable latency for >8k context but increased peak memory for GPU hosts; 64KB pages reduce peak but increased page-churn overhead, causing 4–7% latency variance p95. No measurable semantic quality regressions.
- Continuous batching (15ms window): significant unit-cost improvement for high-concurrency workloads (15–30% tokens/sec gains), but under low QPS this introduced request queuing visible to p50 latency (+6ms). No deterministic quality diffs, but rare timing-sensitive race produced truncated responses in 2 runs out of 1200 due to an edge-case buffer flush (ticket JIRA-ML-4189).

Experimental setup:
- Models: onboarding harness used Llama-2-13B (FP16/4-bit quant variants), and a smaller internal rwin-7B as control.
- Datasets / prompt sets: 1) convo-continuation (420 prompts, variable long-tail context up to 16k tokens), 2) instruction-suite (320 instruction->response prompts), 3) regression-pair-set (120 targeted failure cases from previous kernel changes).
- Eval metrics: token-level next-token accuracy (for continuation), ROUGE-L and BLEU on instruction-suite, embedding-cosine similarity on paraphrase consistency, and application-level heuristics (response truncation, repeated-token rate).
- Infra: A100-40GB nodes for main runs, 8-run seed sweep per config. Baseline: runtime v1.9.2 (pre-kernel changes). Candidate: runtime v2.0-kernel-branch.

Detailed diffs (selected):
1) FlashAttention v2
- Config: enabled flash_v2 flag, mixed-precision reorder ON, kernel patch a1b2c (GH PR 7890).
- Performance: short seq (<=512) token/sec +22% (median), p50 latency -12%.
- Quality: on convo-continuation next-token accuracy baseline 0.742 -> 0.735 (delta -0.9%). Instruction-suite ROUGE-L stable within +/-0.2 points.
- Repro notes: regression reproducible when dropout seed is not fully deterministic across microkernel path. Repro steps: run convo-continuation with seed fixed (env KERNEL_RNG=det) vs default; regression disappears with deterministic seed.
- Mitigation: patch microkernel to copy seed state across reorder path (PR queued). Short-term: add runtime flag flash-attn-legacy-seed-compat to force old codepath.

2) Paged KV cache
- Configs: page_size=64KB and page_size=256KB tested; eviction policy LRU with prefetch disabled for test.
- Performance: for very long contexts (>8k) 256KB reduced p95 latency variance by ~30% compared to 64KB; 64KB increased overall active set memory thrash on bursty workloads causing p95 spikes (+7%).
- Quality: no semantic diffs across evals (cosine similarities delta < 0.002). However, under extreme churn 64KB path triggered a corner-case GC that left stale pointers causing one instance of response corruption (JIRA-ML-4123).
- Resource tradeoff: 256KB favored for Dedicated where memory headroom guaranteed; 64KB better for constrained Private nodes to cap peak memory.
- Recommendation: default page_size=256KB for hosted/dedicated, expose config override for Private with guidance doc. Queue a follow-up to implement adaptive page sizing.

3) Continuous batching (15ms window)
- Config: continuous_batch_window_ms=15, min_batch_tokens=64. Compared with baseline (no continuous batching).
- Performance: for workloads with >200 concurrent RPS, tokens/sec +18–30% depending on sequence length distribution. p50 latency slightly improved for high QPS; for low QPS (<=5 RPS) p50 increased by ~6ms due to intentional micro-queueing.
- Quality: deterministic quality metrics unchanged; however observed two truncation events (edge-case buffer flush bug) producing 1–2 token truncations. Repro repository: run instruction-suite with intermittent tiny timeouts to reproduce.
- Fix: adjust flush ordering and introduce per-request watchdog to avoid premature buffer truncation (PR in progress). Short-term: for Private deployments allow tuning continuous_batch_window_ms to 0 to disable.

Regression matrix (summary, positive means improvement):
- FlashAttention v2: latency: + (improve), throughput: +, next-token-accuracy: -0.9% (regression), truncation events: 0
- Paged KV (256KB): latency stability: +, peak memory: +, semantic-quality: ~0
- Paged KV (64KB): latency stability: -, peak memory: -, semantic-quality: ~0, rare corruption: yes
- Continuous batching (15ms): tokens/sec: +, p50 at low QPS: -, truncations: rare (2/1200)

Action items and owners:
- Priya Sharma (owner): prioritize deterministic RNG seed fix in flash-attn microkernel. Patch PR + test harness by 2025-03-08.
- Ethan Cole: extend long-context convo-continuation prompt set by +200 cases to stress paged-kv and run adaptive page-sizing prototype (due 2025-03-15).
- María Fernández: update onboarding docs to add page_size guidance and continuous batching flags for Private installs (PR by 2025-03-05).
- Ben Liu: add a synthetic load test to replicate low-QPS queuing behavior for continuous batching and add alerting for truncation rate >0.1% (JIRA-ML-4189).

Risk assessment and rollout strategy:
- FlashAttention v2: medium risk because of measurable next-token accuracy delta on long-context conversational workloads. Recommend gated rollout: enable in Hosted for non-critical models behind canary policy, disable by default in Dedicated until seed-fix merged and validated on extended prompt sets.
- Paged KV: low-to-medium risk; choose 256KB default for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private customers, require opt-in with guidance. Adaptive sizing feature would reduce risk long term.
- Continuous batching: low risk for high-QPS customers (clear perf wins). For low-QPS or latency-sensitive workloads, leave disabled by default; expose enablement flag in Console and SDK.

Appendix A — sample failing prompt (convo-continuation) that demonstrates flash-attn regression:
- Context: ~9.6k tokens of dialogue, truncated system message present, follow-up question expecting exact named entity recall.
- Baseline next-token continuation: "...and so the correct answer is Mount Erebus, because..."
- FlashAttn-v2 next-token output: "...and so the correct answer is Mount Ereb" (cut off one token, wrong final token). Behaviour disappears when KERNEL_RNG deterministic.

Appendix B — CI & repro commands:
- Repro baseline: python experiments/run_onboarding_eval.py --model llama-2-13b --runtime v1.9.2 --prompts datasets/convo-continuation.json --seed 42
- Candidate repro: python experiments/run_onboarding_eval.py --model llama-2-13b --runtime v2.0-kernel-branch --enable-flash-v2 --prompts datasets/convo-continuation.json
- Long-run: ./scripts/loadtest.sh --clients 400 --window 15 --profile tokens-per-second --nodes a100-40GB

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally a working/regression report: contains incomplete diagnostics and candidate mitigations. Please add test cases to convo-continuation set if you have known long-context failure modes.
- When approving any kernel change to onboard a model for enterprise customers, we require: (a) no unexplained semantic regression on onboarding prompt sets, (b) mitigations for any truncation/corruption bug, (c) clear rollout flags in Console and SDK.

History and timeline:
- 2025-02-12: initial kernel branch cut (internal).
- 2025-02-18: first sweep ran (this doc created).
- 2025-02-25: intermittent truncation observed during continuous-batching tests.
- 2025-02-28: flash-attn seed-related repro found.
- 2025-03-02: first draft fixes proposed; review in progress.
